title: About me
text: Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, I was immersed in nature from an early age. In turn, outside of being a statistics, data science, and forestry educator and researcher, many of my passions relate to spending time outdoors. Some of my hobbies include exploring new places with my dog (“Dude”, pictured below), cycling, camping, and trying my best to perfect my home espresso skills and technique.

title: Research
text: My research interests lie in small area estimation, hierarchical Bayesian modeling, survey statistics, statistical software, and computing. I am broadly interested in statistical problems motivated by applications to forestry and forest inventory and in answering authentically-motivated research questions from the USDA Forest Service. Central themes in my research include developing novel estimation methods for environmental data and developing simulation-based techniques for the formal evaluation of statistical estimators. I strive to increase practical impact of my research via the development of statistical software such as R packages and interactive dashboards.

title: Teaching
text: As an educator I aim to create an inclusive, safe, welcoming, and productive space for students to engage deeply with statistics and data science concepts. I strive to help students gain confidence in their mathematical, statistical, and programmatic skills by making my courses feel accessible and welcoming, genuinely engaging with questions and feedback from students, and adapting my practices based on continued experience in the classroom.

Other experience

Further, as an undergraduate at Reed College I was a Course Assistant and Tutor for Math 141: Introduction to Probability and Statistics, Math 241: Data Science, Math 392: Mathematical Statistics, and Econ 311: Survey of Econometric Methods.

title: Grayson White
text:
I am a Visiting Assistant Professor of Statistics at Reed College.
My research interests are in small area estimation, survey statistics, hierarchical Bayesian modeling, statistical software, and computing. I am broadly interested in statistical problems motivated by applications to forestry and forest inventory, and have strong ongoing collaborations with the USDA Forest Service, Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) program, who have funded many of my research projects and student research mentorship.
I have a passion for teaching data science and statistics, and for mentoring undergraduate students on research projects. During the summer, I co-direct the Undergraduate Forestry Data Science Lab, a program funded by the Forest Inventory and Analysis program of the U.S. Forest Service where undergraduate students get unique and enriching research experiences in statistics, data science, and forestry. Further, I wholeheartedly believe in the benefits and impact of statistical software for teaching, learning, and research. I’ve developed R packages for teaching statistics, as a result of research with undergraduates and for implementing methodological research. I also maintain an R package with my collaborators from the U.S. Forest Service, FIESTA, which is used for both internally and externally for forest inventory estimation projects and research.
